mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined in each of the last four weekly means (-8.7 to -12.3). This autoregressive momentum reflects persistent behavioral withdrawal from discretionary trips and will continue to push RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks absent a reversing shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell monotonically over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28 days despite four consecutive weeks of prior decline, falsifying pure momentum persistence.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has collapsed from +20.3 to -8.0 over four weeks, signaling a seasonal shift from outdoor to indoor leisure as weather cools. This substitution should raise indoor retail-and-recreation visits once PARKS crosses into negative territory.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from positive to negative week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS turned negative at t-0w after being +20.3 at t-3w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or stays flat for two weeks after PARKS turns negative, indicating no indoor substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT have both declined over the snapshot window (WORKPLACES -13.6 to -12.1 with a trough of -22.7; TRANSIT -17.7 to -22.3). Their joint suppression indicates reduced commuting-linked trip chaining, which historically depresses adjacent retail footfall captured in RETAIL_REC over a full month.
evidence_refs: fact:both series remain substantially negative through t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain jointly depressed, indicating decoupling of commute-linked trip chaining from retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen steadily (2.7 to 4.0) while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain suppressed, consistent with renewed caution or informal restriction-like behavior ahead of winter. In such a tightening regime, people reduce non-essential outings, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises for 3+ consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES stays below -10
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL increased in all four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises despite continued RESIDENTIAL increase and suppressed WORKPLACES, indicating the precautionary-behavior mechanism does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed persistently elevated (9.3 to 11.9) while RETAIL_REC has fallen, suggesting households are substituting essential shopping for discretionary retail-and-recreation trips. This substitution pattern should persist and keep RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above +8 while RETAIL_REC declines for 3 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed in 9-12 range while RETAIL_REC fell from -8.7 to -12.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC recovers while GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated, showing no persistent essential-vs-discretionary substitution.

mechanism_narrative: The decision point falls in mid-November, immediately preceding the holiday shopping season. Historically, retail-and-recreation mobility rises in the four weeks leading into major holidays regardless of recent short-term declines, due to calendar-driven shopping demand.
candidate_trigger: calendar date falls within pre-holiday shopping window (mid-November to December)
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2021-11-15, within the pre-holiday shopping period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues its downward trend through the pre-holiday period, indicating no seasonal holiday-driven uplift.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has fallen sharply, reaching -22.3 at t-0w, a level consistent with renewed public caution or localized restrictions on crowded transit use. When TRANSIT drops below -20 for two consecutive weeks, this typically foreshadows a near-term pullback in retail-and-recreation visits as broader caution spreads.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -20 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -21.6 and -22.3 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks despite TRANSIT remaining below -20, rejecting the transit-caution spillover mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL time has increased every week in the snapshot (2.7 to 4.0), directly indicating more time spent at home. As a near-immediate leading indicator, a rising RESIDENTIAL reading in the most recent week should translate within one week into a modest further dip in RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose in all four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week immediately following a RESIDENTIAL increase, contradicting the short-horizon leading-indicator claim.
